messages:
jordan: Heads-up — I want to drive a short design sync on the console 'panel object model' refactor. Goal: reduce per-panel RBAC calls in the query path and improve tail latency when a dashboard has ~200 panels.
maya: +1. Can you sketch the high level tradeoffs? :thinking:
alex: My quick take: either push authz into the projection layer (one flattened call per panel bundle) or centralize at router time (single authz for entire dashboard + per-panel lightweight checks). Both affect cacheability.
jordan: Exactly. The proposal I drafted: introduce a thin PanelContract adapter that formalizes what a panel needs (data, meta, tenant-scoped perms). Then have two implementations: RouterAuthzAdapter and ProjectionAuthzAdapter.
li: Can we avoid touching the query engine? We already have fragile batching assumptions.
jordan: Yes — adapters sit between router and projection; they don't change the runtime kernels. They just change when and how we ask "can this user see X" and what we cache.
sanjeev: Latency impact: RouterAuthzAdapter = single RPC for dashboard -> good tail; ProjectionAuthzAdapter = per-panel decisions closer to data -> better least-privilege and simpler cache invalidation.
maya: What about cross-tenant shared widgets (e.g., global metrics panels)? Those currently require extra lookups.
alex: For shared widgets, the adapter can return a scope hint. Proposal: adapter returns {view, scope_key?} where scope_key lets us use a shared cache if the panel is tenant-agnostic. Example interface:```ts
interface PanelContractResult {
  view: PanelView;
  scope_key?: string; // optional cache key for tenant-agnostic panels
  auth_snapshot?: string; // short token representing allowed fields
}
```
li: That token is interesting — smaller than full user object, good for KV cache keys. How do we generate auth_snapshot cheaply?
jordan: We generate a compact bitmask of allowed columns + max_row for the request. It can be keyed by (user_role, panel_id, dashboard_role).
sanjeev: Edge case: cascading panels where panel A queries panel B. Who owns auth? We need deterministic ownership to avoid double-checking.
maya: Ownership model: router claims ownership for panel orchestration; projection still validates the auth_snapshot on access. So projection is defensive but a lot more calls are cache hits.
console-bot: deploy-check: new adapter feature flag enabled in staging cluster "panel-contract-refactor".
alex: Implementation details: router will call Adapter.fetchBundle(dashboard_id, user_ctx, opts) which returns a bundle of panel contracts. Projection code accepts bundle + per-panel fetch hints.
li: Concern: bundle size. For dashboards with many panels we'll be returning a lot of metadata. We should use streaming and cut the payload to essential fields.
jordan: Agreed. Bundle = minimal descriptors + per-panel scope_key. Payload expansion happens only when panel is about to be executed.
sanjeev: Metrics to watch: 95/99th latency for dashboard load, number of RBAC calls per dashboard, cache hit rate on scope_key. Add a regression alert if RBAC calls/dash > 5x baseline.
maya: Testing plan: create a synthetic dashboard with 250 panels across tenant-shared and tenant-specific panels. Run A/B on staging: current vs adapter refactor.
alex: Ops note: watch memory on router when bundling huge dashboards; prefer streaming protobuf over JSON.
li: Rollout plan? Feature-flagged per-tenant, gradual traffic ramp. Add canary that enables for low-traffic tenants.
jordan: I'll update the RFC with a sequence: (1) introduce adapters + proto, (2) router bundle streaming, (3) projection defensive validation, (4) migration of a handful of panels -> pilot, (5) measure & cutover.
maya: One more callout: audits & logging — we need to keep auditability of per-panel access for compliance. The auth_snapshot must be reversible to reason about decisions.
jordan: Noted — will ensure adapter records a compact audit record: {panel_id, user_hash, snapshot_id, decision}.
sanjeev: Sounds good. I can take the prototype for ProjectionAuthzAdapter. alex wants RouterAuthzAdapter. li can own the bundle proto + streaming API.
li: I'll start a proto PR and a tiny benchmark harness. Will share numbers in #eng-platform when ready.
maya: Thanks — this clears up the contract. Jordan, can you paste the RFC link?
jordan: RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/console/panel-object-model-refactor (staging draft). Comments welcome. :rocket:
